# Unemployment Rate among Highly-Educated Immigrant Women by the Country of Destination

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(tinytex)
```

## PART I: Clean data

### Data Source

The data used in this study come from the OECD Data Explorer: [https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?lc=en&df%5Bds%5D=dsDisseminateFinalDMZ&df%5Bid%5D=DSD_EAG_LSO_EA%40DF_LSO_NEAC_UNEMP_MIGR&df%5Bag%5D=OECD.EDU.IMEP&dq=AUS%2BAUT%2BBEL%2BCAN%2BCHL%2BCOL%2BCRI%2BCZE%2BEST%2BFRA%2BDEU%2BGRC%2BHUN%2BIRL%2BITA%2BLVA%2BLTU%2BLUX%2BMEX%2BNLD%2BNZL%2BNOR%2BPOL%2BPRT%2BSVK%2BSVN%2BESP%2BSWE%2BCHE%2BGBR%2BUSA%2BBGR%2BROU.M%2BF.Y25T34%2BY35T44%2BY55T64%2BY45T54%2BY25T64.ISCED11A_0T2%2BISCED11A_3_4%2BISCED11A_5T8....NB%2BFB......OBS...A3&lom=LASTNOBSERVATIONS&lo=1&pd=2023,2023&to%5BTIME_PERIOD%5D=true&lb=nm&vw=ov](#0){.uri}

```{r}
raw_data <- read_csv("/Users/chihhsuan/Desktop/UBC 26W/SOCI 502/SOCI502_data_story/data/raw_data_1027.csv")
```

```{r}
names(raw_data)
```

### Step 1: Cleaning the sex variable

The original SEX variable uses the codes F and M, which are recoded into female and male for readability.

```{r}
raw_data |> count(SEX)

clean_data <- 
  raw_data |>
  mutate(sex = case_when(
    SEX == "F" ~ "female",
    SEX == "M" ~ "male"
  )) |>
  select(-SEX, -any_of("Sex")) #刪掉原本的代碼欄和標籤欄以避免重複

count(clean_data, sex)
```

### Step 2: Cleaning the age variable

The original AGE variable uses codes such as Y25T34, which are recoded into readable age groups: 25–34. The code Y25T64 represents the total for all four age groups and is recoded as 25–64. The age groups are ordered from youngest to oldest.

```{r}
raw_data |> count(AGE)

clean_data <- 
  clean_data  |>
  mutate(age = case_when(
    AGE == "Y25T34" ~ "25-34",
    AGE == "Y35T44" ~ "35-44",
    AGE == "Y45T54" ~ "45-54",
    AGE == "Y55T64" ~ "55-64",
    AGE == "Y25T64" ~ "25-64"
  )) |>
  mutate(age = factor(age, levels = c("25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "25-64")))

count(clean_data, age)
```

### Step 3: Cleaning the educational attainment variable

The original ATTAINMENT_LEV variable uses ISCED 2011 codes, which are recoded into three categories: below upper secondary (ISCED11A_0T2), upper secondary (ISCED11A_3_4) and tertiary (ISCED11A_5T8)

```{r}
raw_data |> count(ATTAINMENT_LEV)

# 教育程度
clean_data <- 
  clean_data |>
  mutate(edu = case_when(
    ATTAINMENT_LEV == "ISCED11A_0T2" ~ "below upper secondary",
    ATTAINMENT_LEV == "ISCED11A_3_4" ~ "upper secondary",
    ATTAINMENT_LEV == "ISCED11A_5T8" ~ "tertiary"
  )) |>
  mutate(edu = factor(edu, levels = c("below upper secondary", "upper secondary", "tertiary")))

count(clean_data, edu)
```

### Step 4: Cleaning the country variable

The original REF_AREA variable uses three-letter country codes, which are converted into full country names (for example, CAN becomes Canada).

```{r}
raw_data |> count(REF_AREA)

# 國家對照表
country_names <- c(
  AUS = "Australia", AUT = "Austria", BEL = "Belgium", BGR = "Bulgaria",
  CAN = "Canada", CHE = "Switzerland", CHL = "Chile", COL = "Colombia",
  CRI = "Costa Rica", CZE = "Czechia", DEU = "Germany", ESP = "Spain",
  EST = "Estonia", FRA = "France", GBR = "United Kingdom", GRC = "Greece",
  HUN = "Hungary", IRL = "Ireland", ISR = "Israel", ITA = "Italy",
  LTU = "Lithuania", LUX = "Luxembourg", LVA = "Latvia", MEX = "Mexico",
  NLD = "Netherlands", NOR = "Norway", NZL = "New Zealand", 
  POL = "Poland", PRT = "Portugal", ROU = "Romania", SVK = "Slovak Republic",
  SVN = "Slovenia", SWE = "Sweden", USA = "United States"
)

# 國家
clean_data <- 
  clean_data |>
  mutate(country = unname(country_names[REF_AREA]))

count(clean_data, country)
```

### Step 5: Cleaning the birthplace variable

The original BIRTH_PLACE variable uses the codes NB and FB, which are recoded into native-born and foreign-born.

```{r}
raw_data |> count(BIRTH_PLACE)

clean_data <- 
  clean_data  |>
  mutate(birth = case_when(
    BIRTH_PLACE == "NB" ~ "native-born",
    BIRTH_PLACE == "FB" ~ "foreign-born"
  ))

count(clean_data, birth)
```

### Step 6: Cleaning the unemployment rate variable (the outcome variable of this study)

The original OBS_VALUE variable is renamed unemp_rate. It is already stored as a numeric value and is measured as a percentage of the labor force in each subgroup, so no further conversion is needed.

```{r}
count(raw_data, MEASURE, UNIT_MEASURE)
clean_data <-
  clean_data |>
  rename(unemp_rate = OBS_VALUE)
```

### Step 7: Keeping only the cleaned variables

```{r}
# 只保留整理好的變項
clean_data <-
  clean_data |>
  filter(MIGRATION_AGE %in% c("_Z", "_T")) |>
  select(country, sex, age, edu, birth, unemp_rate)
```

### Step 8: Coding countries by region

Each country is assigned to one of seven regions: North America, Latin America, Oceania, Western Europe, Northern Europe, Southern Europe and Eastern Europe.

```{r}
# 地區對照表
region_names <- c(
  "Canada" = "North America", "United States" = "North America",
  "Chile" = "Latin America", "Colombia" = "Latin America",
  "Costa Rica" = "Latin America", "Mexico" = "Latin America",
  "Australia" = "Oceania", "New Zealand" = "Oceania",
  "Austria" = "Eastern Europe", "Belgium" = "Western Europe",
  "France" = "Western Europe", "Germany" = "Western Europe",
  "Ireland" = "Western Europe", "Luxembourg" = "Western Europe",
  "Netherlands" = "Western Europe", "Switzerland" = "Western Europe",
  "United Kingdom" = "Western Europe",
  "Norway" = "Northern Europe", "Sweden" = "Northern Europe",
  "Greece" = "Southern Europe", "Italy" = "Southern Europe",
  "Portugal" = "Southern Europe", "Spain" = "Southern Europe",
  "Bulgaria" = "Eastern Europe", "Czechia" = "Eastern Europe",
  "Estonia" = "Eastern Europe", "Hungary" = "Eastern Europe",
  "Latvia" = "Eastern Europe", "Lithuania" = "Eastern Europe",
  "Poland" = "Eastern Europe", "Romania" = "Eastern Europe",
  "Slovak Republic" = "Eastern Europe", "Slovenia" = "Eastern Europe"
)

# 地區
clean_data <-
  clean_data |>
  mutate(region = unname(region_names[country]),
         region = factor(region, levels = c("North America", "Latin America", "Oceania",
                                            "Western Europe", "Northern Europe",
                                            "Southern Europe", "Eastern Europe")))
```

```{r}
head(clean_data)
```

## PART II: Tests

### Test1: This test checks that the recoded categorical variables (country, sex, age, education and birthplace) contain no missing values.

```{r}
sum(is.na(clean_data$sex)) == 0
sum(is.na(clean_data$age)) == 0
sum(is.na(clean_data$edu)) == 0
sum(is.na(clean_data$birth)) == 0
sum(is.na(clean_data$country)) == 0
```

### Test2: Since each combination of country, sex, age, education and birthplace should appear in only one row, this test checks that no combination is duplicated.

```{r}
clean_data |>
  count(country, sex, age, edu, birth) |>
  filter(n > 1)
```

```{r}
write_csv(clean_data, "/Users/chihhsuan/Desktop/UBC 26W/SOCI 502/SOCI502_data_story/data/clean_data.csv")
```
